message.content:
Let the polar curve be given by

\[
r=\cos\theta+\frac12.
\]

The \(x\)-coordinate of a polar point \((r,\theta)\) is

\[
x=r\cos\theta.
\]

Substitute \(r=\cos\theta+\frac12\):

\[
x=\left(\cos\theta+\frac12\right)\cos\theta
=\cos^2\theta+\frac12\cos\theta.
\]

Let \(c=\cos\theta\). Since \(-1\le c\le 1\), we need to minimize

\[
x=c^2+\frac12 c.
\]

Complete the square:

\[
x=\left(c+\frac14\right)^2-\frac1{16}.
\]

The minimum occurs when

\[
c=-\frac14,
\]

which is possible because \(-1\le -\frac14\le 1\). Thus the smallest \(x\)-coordinate is

\[
-\frac1{16}.
\]

The answer is \(\boxed{-\frac1{16}}\).
